Ruthenium-Catalyzed α-Regioselective Hydroboration of Allenes
Yun-Xuan Tan<sup>+</sup>, Shijia Li<sup>+</sup>, Liang Chen, Jing Huang, Chaoshen Zhang, Lijuan Song,*
Xinhao Zhang, Yun-Dong Wu,* and Jianwei Sun*
Abstract: Hydroboration of allenes is powerful and
atom-economic approach to the synthesis of organo-
boranes, such as the highly versatile allylboranes.
However, regarding regiocontrol, existing methods uni-
formly deliver the boron functionality to the less
hindered β- or γ-position, but not the α-position. The
latter is particularly challenging for allenes with sub-
stantial steric difference between the two terminals and
lacking electronic bias (e.g., 1,1-disubstituted allenes).
Herein we report the first highly efficient ruthenium-
catalyzed hydroboration of allenes featuring exclusive α-
regioselectivity, providing access to sterically hindered
allyl boranes that are limitedly accessible by conven-
tional methods. DFT studies suggested that the unusual
α-regioselectivity is attributed to the disfavored reduc-
tive elimination at the γ-position due to the high energy
cost required to overcome the agostic interaction and
rotation of the key π-allyl intermediates. This protocol is
also applicable to the previously unprecedented α-
hydroalkynylation and underdeveloped α-hydrosilyla-
tion of allenes, thus complementing known catalytic
systems and providing convenient access to highly
congested yet densely-functionalized allyl silanes and
skipped enynes bearing a fully-substituted allylic carbon
center. It is expected that this ruthenium-catalyzed
system can serve as a new platform for the development
of other hydrofunctionalization processes with unortho-
dox selectivity.

A gram-scale experiment of 1 a was carried out at 40 °C
(Scheme 2b). No obvious loss of chemical efficiency was
observed even when the catalyst loading was reduced to
0.125 mol%. To further illustrate the synthetic application

boronate product 2a were conducted. The selective oxida-

Inspired by the high α-regioselectivity observed in hydro-
boration, we were curious whether this protocol can be
applied to other allene hydrofunctionalizations to achieve
the same unusual selectivity. To gain more information
about the feasibility, we first studied the kinetic and
thermodynamic features of the α-selective reductive elimi-
nation step for those potential functionalizations, including
hydroalkynylation, hydrosilylation, hydroamination, and
hydroalkylation (Table 2). Our DFT results indicated that
the reductive elimination steps are all thermodynamically
favorable, leading to relatively more stable products. More-

tion (entries 2–3) exhibit reasonable stability when
compared with the hydroboration counterparts (entry 1),
suggesting high feasibility of these two processes. In
contrast, the related intermediates and transition states for
hydroalkylation and hydroamination (entries 4–5) are much
higher in energy, alluding that the formation of the key
complexes is already difficult, let alone the subsequent
reductive elimination.
Encouraged by the above preliminary theoretical data,
we chose to investigate the more feasible hydroalkynylation

decades, efficient protocols remain limitedly available.<sup>[20]</sup>

addition regioselectivity leading to conjugated enyne prod-

observed even without modification of the standard con-
ditions, in sharp contrast to the uniform β-selectivity

Conclusion
α-Regioselective hydrofunctionalization of allenes that deliv-
ers a functionality to the sterically hindered position
represents a general challenge in organic synthesis, which is
particularly true for allenes with substantially unfavorable
steric difference and lacking electronic bias. Here we have
developed a highly efficient and general protocol of this
type enabled by a uniquely effective ruthenium catalyst,
[Cp*RuCl] , with exclusive α-regioselectivity. This protocol
is not only applicable to the previously unprecedented α-
hydroboration and α-hydroalkynylation of allenes, but also
complementary to the limitedly available α-hydrosilylation
approaches that require less bulky substrates. Thus, a range
of sterically hindered allyl boranes, skipped enynes, and allyl
silanes bearing a fully-substituted allylic carbon center were
generated with high efficiency and selectivity under mild
conditions. It is worth noting that these highly congested yet
densely-functionalized synthetic blocks were limitedly acces-
sible before by conventional methods (often requiring multi-
ple steps and/or special reagents), but they can be made with
ease and atom-economy from simple substrates by our
protocol. The mild conditions are compatible with a range
of functional groups. DFT studies provided important
insights into the reaction mechanism. The high α-regioselec-
tivity is attributed to the blocked direct reductive elimina-
tion at the more accessible γ-position, which is disfavored by
the high energy cost resulting from either agostic interaction
or rotation of the key π-allyl intermediates. Further detailed
investigations on the reaction mechanism as well as the
extension of this protocol to other hydrofunctionalization
processes with unorthodox selectivity are ongoing in our
laboratory.
